clue.text: Started for instance, during Prohibition

indicators.note: during places the example abbreviation within the ban, as something happening inside a period

parts.note: a prohibition is a ban

explanation.surface: Something got going in the Prohibition era, as an example of bootlegging days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prohibition' with a capital suggests the American era, but here it is simply a ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Began is the simple past of begin, a straight synonym for started.

clue.text: Seize some eggs

explanation.surface: A command to grab a handful of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab hold of is to clutch; a clutch is also a set of eggs laid at one time.

clue.text: Shut up tight in the terminus

indicators.note: in signals that the word for tight sits inside the word for the terminus

parts.note: a terminus is the end of the line
close can mean tight, as in a close fit

explanation.surface: Someone stuck fast at the end of the line, locked up at the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up tight' looks like one phrase, but 'tight' is the piece that goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shut up means being confined, closed in on all sides.

clue.text: Slander Parsees badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of the following word are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone speaks ill of the Parsi community.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to cast damaging, false aspersions, a formal synonym for slander.

clue.text: Murder a number in odd surroundings

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, tells us the number goes inside the word for odd
surroundings means the word for odd wraps around the number

parts.note: odd means strange
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so a number

explanation.surface: A killing in which a number of victims are found in peculiar circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is a crossword favourite for a Roman numeral; here L, fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is a way to kill someone by choking, a specific kind of killing.

clue.text: Seem to enjoy swilling a double

indicators.note: swilling suggests the two words wash around the little a, holding it in the middle

parts.note: look can mean seem, as in to look happy
to like something is to enjoy it

explanation.surface: Someone appears to enjoy knocking back a double measure of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' is not a measure of spirits but a person's twin; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is someone who closely resembles another person, a doppelganger.

clue.text: Fault admitted by assistant returning to stock up

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled run is read backwards
admitted by means the word for fault is let inside the word for assistant

parts.note: an assistant is a helper
a sin is a moral fault

explanation.surface: An assistant comes back to restock after owning up to a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assistant' is HELPER; 'admitted by' and 'returning' work on the whole thing, so build it first and read it backwards. 'Stock up' is the definition, with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to refill, which is what stocking up does to supplies.

clue.text: Was standing on the street with nothing to do in retirement

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in retirement suggests drawing back, so the word do is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired person stood about on the street with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Stood is the past tense of stand, matching was standing.

clue.text: Merit award in best artistic category

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the words best artistic

explanation.surface: A prize for merit given in the best artistic category.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold star is a classic reward for good work.

clue.text: Work in vile prison

indicators.note: in means the word for work is placed inside the word for vile

parts.note: base means low and vile
to till is to work the soil

explanation.surface: Labour in a dreadful jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the verb till, as in working land.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress prison stormed in 1789; the word also means any prison.

clue.text: One is going to make them

definitions.text: One is going to make them

parts.words: One is going to make them
parts.note: anyone going somewhere on foot leaves footprints and trails behind

explanation.surface: Someone setting out is bound to leave a trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' reads as intention, but it is literal travel leaving marks; also the idiom to make tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracks are the marks or trails a moving person or animal leaves.

clue.text: Resistance units initially on her Majesty's service

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: Official government business is conducted at a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: OHMS, On Her Majesty's Service, is printed on British official mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.

clue.text: Try hard to get free labour

explanation.surface: A prisoner exerts themselves to escape and do unpaid work.
explanation.definitionFit: To struggle is to strain to break loose; a struggle is also hard toil.

clue.text: Forbore to put artist in cultural surroundings

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, places the artist inside the word for cultural
surroundings means the cultural word wraps around the artist

parts.note: refined means cultured and cultivated
RA, Royal Academician, is a common abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: Someone held back from placing a painter among sophisticated people.
explanation.definitionFit: Refrained and forbore are both past tenses meaning held oneself back.

clue.text: They may be required to be met

definitions.text: They may be required to be met

parts.words: They may be required to be met
parts.note: things required of someone, such as claims or ultimatums, are things one meets or satisfies

explanation.surface: People who must be greeted on arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' suggests greeting visitors; you meet a requirement by satisfying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demands are requests or claims that must be satisfied.

clue.text: Predecessor leaving no traces around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Whoever came before left no evidence behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' is a link here; 'around' rearranges NO TRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, someone from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Bacon's lines

parts.note: a rasher of bacon has bands of fat running through it

explanation.surface: Verses by Francis Bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital points to the philosopher Francis Bacon, but this is bacon on the plate, as in streaky bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaks are thin lines or bands of colour, like those in streaky bacon.

clue.text: It is involved with change in education

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are tangled together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that education involves change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' mixes IT with CHANGE; 'is' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching is instruction, the work of educating others.

clue.text: Lace with gin perhaps, it's divine!

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A cocktail of gin is praised as heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' looks like a verb for spiking a drink, but its letters join GIN to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means heavenly or saintly, like an angel.

clue.text: A bit vulgar, perhaps?

parts.note: a part of a whole written as one number over another is called vulgar in arithmetic

explanation.surface: Something mildly crude.
explanation.walkthrough: A vulgar fraction is a common fraction such as three quarters; 'a bit' is a part.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraction is a part or portion of a whole.

clue.text: Metal press

explanation.surface: A metal press.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is a metallic element; to press clothes smooth is to iron them.

clue.text: A record, second highest in the European charts

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A single climbs to number two on the Euro music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charts' suggests music, but these are maps showing the highest mountains of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are the highest mountain range wholly in western Europe.

clue.text: European may be French

explanation.surface: A European person might be French.
explanation.walkthrough: French polish is a shellac varnish for furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish describes someone from Poland; French polish is one kind of wood finish.

clue.text: Private lodging provided with little hesitation

parts.note: an inn provides lodging
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Private lodgings offered with barely a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner means internal or personal, as in one's private, inner thoughts.

clue.text: A failure if returning as a company

indicators.note: returning means the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm would be a flop if it came back as a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating disaster, a complete failure.

clue.text: Troops stepped out in these formations

definitions.text: Troops stepped out in these formations

parts.words: Troops stepped out in these formations
parts.note: soldiers arranged so each line is staggered from the next, like steps

explanation.surface: Soldiers marching out on parade in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stepped out' suggests marching, but describes a staggered, step-like arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a military formation with units staggered one behind another.

clue.text: Devil doctor in his study

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the word for his study

parts.note: a den is a private study or retreat
MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A fiendish doctor lurks in his study.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit, a fiend.

clue.text: Sees sense maybe, within reason

indicators.note: within means the reworked word sits inside the word for reason

parts.note: one's wits are one's reason, good sense

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters of sense could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone finally comes to their senses, within reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' gives NESSE from the clue word; 'Sees' is the verb, not a plural, and 'reason' is one's wits.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it happen.
